title: Lexical Limitation
definition: The limitation in relevance-based keyword matching that arises from differences in lexical representation between disciplines, such as the use of Sanskrit terms in Buddhist philosophy versus English in popular culture.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine trying to find a recipe written in French using only English words. You might not find the perfect match, even if the idea is there.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Lexical limitations in keyword matching can lead to missed connections between disciplines due to differences in lexical representation. This is common in cross-cultural and cross-linguistic contexts.
difficulty_levels.expert: Lexical limitations in keyword matching highlight the complexities of cross-disciplinary information retrieval. To overcome these limitations, we can explore semantic and contextual similarity measures that go beyond lexical overlap. This can involve techniques like word embeddings and transformer models.

extra_fields.insight: The limitations of lexical matching can result in missed connections between disciplines, even when the concepts are fundamentally the same.
